title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #12
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #12 · Q1
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I
(A) The Poetics of Prose
(B) Problems of Dostoevsky's Poetics
(C) Surprised by Sin
(D) The Way Women Write

List II
(I) Stanley Fish
(II) Tzvetan Todorov
(III) Mikhail Bakhtin
(IV) Mary Hiatt

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The Poetics of Prose (1971) was written by Tzvetan Todorov (A-II), Problems of Dostoevsky's Poetics (1929) by Mikhail Bakhtin (B-III), Surprised by Sin (1967) by Stanley Fish (C-I), and The Way Women Write (1977) by Mary Hiatt (D-IV).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q2
items.stem: Who among the following protagonists of Thomas ardy feels his lot as akin to Job’s ?
items.explanation: In Thomas Hardy's Jude the Obscure (1895), following the murder of his children by Little Father Time and his abandonment by Sue Bridehead, the broken Jude Fawley lies dying on Remembrance Day in Christminster bitterly reciting Job 3 ('Let the day perish wherein I was born').

items.title: Mock #12 · Q3
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory post World War II
items.stem:
Michael ardt and Antonio Negri prefer to use H“Empire” rather than imperialism.
According to them :
options: There is only one empire and we had better recognize it. ence the Empire with E upper case.
There may be many empires but only one is patently visible and operational. That is denoted by Empire with E upper case.
The present day empire does not have an identifiable location or centre. ence we ought to differentiate this view of Empire with E upper case.
The culturally dominant global empire is the only one that really matters. We signify that Empire with E upper case.
items.explanation: In Empire (2000), Michael Hardt and Antonio Negri conceptualize 'Empire' (capitalized) as a decentred, deterritorialized global apparatus of governance without an imperialist national center or border, distinguishing it from historical European imperialism.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q4
items.stem: The arrival of corpus linguistics has revitalized
options: the writing that does not care for grammar.
the use of long sentences in newspaper reporting.
items.explanation: The arrival of corpus linguistics—using large electronic databases of authentic spoken and written texts—has revitalized the writing of empirical, observation-based descriptive grammars (such as the Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q5
items.stem:
Arrange the following novels in the chronological order of their publication:
(A) The White Tiger
(B) A Tiger for Malgudi
(C) A Suitable Boy
(D) Heat and Dust
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Heat and Dust (1975), A Tiger for Malgudi (1983), A Suitable Boy (1993), The White Tiger (2008).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q6
items.stem: Identify the story for which E. M. Forster wrote the libretto for its opera version
items.explanation: Novelist E. M. Forster collaborated with Eric Crozier to write the libretto for composer Benjamin Britten's 1951 four-act opera Billy Budd, adapted from Herman Melville's posthumous novella Billy Budd, Sailor (1924).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement 1: Criticism is the construction of a judgment about the negative or positive qualities of someone or something.
Statement 2: Criticism can be theoretical, practical, impressionistic, affective, prescriptive, or descriptive.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer given below:
options: Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false but Statement 2 is true.
Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are false
Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true.
items.explanation: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true: criticism involves forming an evaluative judgment about the merits or faults of a work, and literary criticism encompasses theoretical, practical, impressionistic, affective, prescriptive, and descriptive approaches.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q8
items.stem: For The Unfallen is a book of poems written by
items.explanation: For the Unfallen: Poems 1952-1958 (1959) is the debut poetry collection of British poet Geoffrey Hill, containing celebrated poems such as 'Genesis' and 'In Memory of Jane Fraser' that explore history, martyrdom, and moral responsibility.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q9
items.stem:
In Ben Jonson's Volpone, the animal
imagery includes

(a)
the fox and the vulture

(b)
the fly and the cockroach

(c)
the fly, the crow and the raven

(d)
the fox, the vulture and the goat
items.explanation: In Ben Jonson's satirical city comedy Volpone (1606), the central characters have Italian names corresponding to animals and birds of prey or carrion: Volpone ('the Fox'), Voltore ('the Vulture'), Mosca ('the Fly'), Corbaccio ('the Raven'), and Corvino ('the Crow'), making (a) and (c) correct.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q10
items.stem:
An English poet couldn't help the excitement that an historical event caused in his
life-time :
Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive,
But to be young was very heaven.
Which poet ?  What "dawn" ?
options: Lord Tennyson ; the Jubilee of Queen Victoria's reign
items.explanation: In Book XI of The Prelude (also published separately in 1809 as 'French Revolution, as It Appeared to Enthusiasts at Its Commencement'), William Wordsworth captured his youthful revolutionary enthusiasm for the dawn of the French Revolution of 1789 with these celebrated lines.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the lines with the titles of the poems :
I.
The boa-constrictor's coil/ Is a fossil
A.
"Thrushes"
II.
My manners are tearing off heads /
The allotment of death
B.
"The Jaguar"
III.
More coiled steel than living
C.
"Relic"
IV.
Time in the sea eats its tail
D.
"Hawk Roosting"

Codes :

I
II
III
IV
items.explanation: All four quotations are from animal poems by Ted Hughes: (I) 'The boa-constrictor's coil / Is a fossil' is from 'The Jaguar' (B); (II) 'My manners are tearing off heads— / The allotment of death' is from 'Hawk Roosting' (D); (III) 'More coiled steel than living' is from 'Thrushes' (A); and (IV) 'Time in the sea eats its tail' is from 'Relic' (C), giving B-D-A-C.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q12
items.stem:
The Restoration comedy has been
criticized mainly for its
items.explanation: From Jeremy Collier's 1698 polemic A Short View of the Immorality, and Profaneness of the English Stage through nineteenth-century Victorian critics like Lord Macaulay, Restoration comedy has been criticized mainly for its sexual indecency, cuckoldry plots, and moral permissiveness.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q13
items.stem:
Choose the correct statements with regard to the binary pair Langue and Parole introduced by Ferdinand de Saussure
A. Langue is translated as speech and parole as language
B. Langue is the internal structure of a language not language itself.
C. Parole is the event of language.
D. Parole and language are a set of vocabulary only
E. There is no distinction between Parole and Langue
items.explanation: In Ferdinand de Saussure's structural linguistics, langue refers to the abstract, underlying rule-governed system and structure of a language (B), while parole refers to the concrete, individualized speech acts and actual events of language use (C). Statement A is incorrect because langue means language/system and parole means speech.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q14
items.stem:
The motto "only connect" is taken
from
options: Wells' The History of Mr. Polly
items.explanation: 'Only connect...' is the celebrated epigraph and central thematic leitmotif of E. M. Forster's novel Howards End (1910), advocating harmony between the pragmatic material world (the Wilcoxes) and the inner life of culture and emotion (the Schlegels).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q15
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their year of publication.
A. Deconstruction and Criticism
B. Multiculturalism: Roots and Realities
C. Literary Theory and the Claims of History
D. The Western Canon
E. An Appetite for Poetry
items.explanation: The publication years of these theoretical works in chronological order are: Deconstruction and Criticism by Harold Bloom, Paul de Man, Jacques Derrida, Geoffrey Hartman, and J. Hillis Miller (1979), Frank Kermode's An Appetite for Poetry (1989), Harold Bloom's The Western Canon (1994), Satya P. Mohanty's Literary Theory and the Claims of History (1997), and C. James Trotman's Multiculturalism: Roots and Realities (2002). This sequence is A -> E -> D -> C -> B.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q16
items.stem: In "An Apology for Poetry" Sidney discusses the didactic function of poetry by comparing it to philosophy and:
items.explanation: In An Apology for Poetry (1595), Sir Philip Sidney argues for the superior didactic power of poetry by comparing the poet with the moral philosopher (who gives abstract precepts) and the historian (who is tied to particular facts).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: A dozen or more distinct languages and literatures flourish today on the Indian literary scene, and most of these are distributed on a broadly regional basis.
Reason R: The Aryans brought Sanskrit to India; the Muslim rule led to the rise of Urdu, as an expression of a composite culture; and the British rule made Indo-Anglian literature possible.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
items.explanation: In K. R. Srinivasa Iyengar's Indian Writing in English, India's diverse regional and pan-Indian literary traditions are explained through historical waves: Sanskrit brought by the Aryans, Urdu emerging under Muslim rule, and Indo-Anglian literature enabled by British rule.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q18
items.stem:
Choose the correct events corresponding with their year
A. The Official Languages Commission submitted its report in 1936.
B. The first ELTI was established in Allahabad in 1954.
C. The Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages was established in Hyderabad in 1958.
D. National Policy on Education came in 1960.
E. The NEP and POA came in 1986.
items.explanation: Statements B, C, and E accurately state milestones in Indian English education: the first ELTI was founded in Allahabad in 1954, CIEFL (now EFLU) was established in Hyderabad in 1958, and the National Policy on Education with its Programme of Action was enacted in 1986. Statement A is false because the Official Language Commission reported in 1956, and statement D is false because India's first NPE was issued in 1968.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q19
items.stem:
"The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" names the following figures:
A. Ezra Pound
B. Michelangelo
C. Valerie Eliot
D. Hamlet
E. Walt Whitman
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: T.S. Eliot's poem 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock' (1915) explicitly names Michelangelo ('In the room the women come and go / Talking of Michelangelo,' B) and Prince Hamlet ('No! I am not Prince Hamlet, nor was meant to be,' D).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q20
items.stem: Who, in "The World as India," argues that English can be the only common "unifying language" of India?
items.explanation: American critic Susan Sontag delivered the 2002 St. Jerome Lecture on literary translation titled 'The World as India' (collected in At the Same Time, 2007), reflecting on English in multilingual India.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q21
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. Basudev Sunani
B. Om Prakash Valmiki
C. Bama
D. Urmila Pawar
I. Karukku
II. Weave of My Life
III. Cast Out
IV. Joothan
items.explanation: Basudev Sunani authored Cast Out (translated from Odia Chhi, 2008) (A-III); Omprakash Valmiki wrote the landmark Hindi Dalit autobiography Joothan (1997) (B-IV); Bama wrote the Tamil Dalit autoethnography Karukku (1992) (C-I); and Urmila Pawar authored the Marathi Dalit feminist memoir The Weave of My Life (Aaidan, 2003) (D-II). This gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q22
items.stem: Why did T. S. Eliot assert that Virgil, not Homer, is the poet of Europe?
options: There are some initial moral concerns in Virgil
Virgil belongs to the Roman period
Homer was a pagan who was a renegade
Virgil wrote in Latin while Homer wrote in Greek
items.explanation: In 'What is a Classic?' Eliot ties Virgil to Rome and its imperial destiny, which shaped Europe's idea of civilisation.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q23
items.stem:
Which two of the following essays form part of Mikhail Bakhtin's The Dialogic Imagination: Four Essays?
A. "From the History of Novelistic Discourse"
B. "Discourse in the Novel"
C. "Romance and Novel"
D. "Forms of Time and the Chronotope in the Novel"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Mikhail Bakhtin's The Dialogic Imagination: Four Essays (edited by Michael Holquist, 1981) contains 'Epic and Novel,' 'From the Prehistory of Novelistic Discourse,' 'Forms of Time and of the Chronotope in the Novel' (D), and 'Discourse in the Novel' (B).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q24
items.stem:
"It ought to be the first endeavour of a writer to distinguish nature from custom, or that which is established because it is right from that which is right only because it is established; that he may neither violate essential principles by a desire of novelty, nor debar himself from the attainment of beauties within his view by a needless fear of breaking rules which no literary dictator had authority to enact".

The above passage considered to be the death-knell of the neo-classical criticism is attributed to ____.
items.explanation: This passage appears in Samuel Johnson's The Rambler, No. 156 (14 September 1751), where Johnson critiques rigid neoclassical rules such as the dramatic unities and distinguishes universal nature from arbitrary literary custom.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q25
items.stem:
Arrange the correct chronological sequence of events that affected literary criticism and theory.
A. Man's First Flight to the Moon
B. End of the World War II
C. Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' Speech
D. Russian Revolution
E. India's Independence
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological sequence of these twentieth-century historical events is: the Russian Revolution (1917, D), the End of World War II (1945, B), India's Independence (1947, E), Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech (1963, C), and Man's First Flight to the Moon (Apollo 11 in 1969, A), giving D, B, E, C, A.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q26
items.stem:
According to coleridge, the “secondary imagination” “dissolves, diffuses, __________, in
order to recreate...”.
Choose the right word for the blank.
items.explanation: In Chapter XIII of Biographia Literaria (1817), Samuel Taylor Coleridge famously defines the secondary imagination as an echo of the primary: 'It dissolves, diffuses, dissipates, in order to recreate; or where this process is rendered impossible, yet still at all events it struggles to idealize and to unify.'

items.title: Mock #12 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: Sidney's Apologie for Poetrie is in many ways a seminal text of literary criticism.
Reason R: It represents the first synthesis in the English language of the various strands and concerns of Renaissance literary criticism, drawing on Aristotle, Horace, and more recent writers such as Boccaccio and Julius Caesar Scaliger.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
items.explanation: As M. A. R. Habib explains in A History of Literary Criticism, Sir Philip Sidney's An Apologie for Poetrie (1595) is a seminal text because it achieved the first English synthesis of Renaissance critical thought drawing on Aristotle, Horace, Boccaccio, and Scaliger.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q28
items.stem:
List – I (Book)
A. The Complete Adventures of Feluda
B. The Perfect Murder
C. Sacred Games
D. Djinn Patrol on the Purple Line
List – II (Author)
I. Vikram Chandra
II. Ruskin Bond
III. Deepa Annapara
IV. Satyajit Ray
items.explanation: Satyajit Ray authored the celebrated detective series featuring Prodosh C. Mitter in The Complete Adventures of Feluda (A-IV); Ruskin Bond edited and wrote crime mystery tales including The Perfect Murder anthology (B-II); Vikram Chandra wrote the acclaimed Mumbai underworld thriller Sacred Games (2006) (C-I); and Deepa Anappara authored the missing-children novel Djinn Patrol on the Purple Line (2020) (D-III).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q29
items.stem:
Which of the following are true in the context of "Phenomenology"?
A. It is "a form of methodological idealism" which seeks to explore 'human consciousness'.
B. As a philosophical method, it was developed by Edmund Husserl.
C. Martin Heidegger is one of its leading philosophers.
D. Martin Heidegger's approach is "essentialist".
E. Text is considered purely as an embodiment of the author's consciousness.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
A, B, C and E only
items.explanation: Phenomenology, founded by Edmund Husserl (B) and developed by Martin Heidegger (C), explores human consciousness (A) and in Geneva School criticism views the text as an embodiment of the author's consciousness (E), whereas Heidegger's existential approach is anti-essentialist (giving Option 3: A, B, C and E only).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q30
items.stem: In Wuthering Heights, Cathy appears in a dream beating at a window, wailing "Let me in", blood running down her wrist. Who dreams her ?
items.explanation: In Chapter 3 of Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights (1847), the new tenant Mr. Lockwood spends a stormy night in Catherine Earnshaw's old oak-panelled bed and has a terrifying nightmare in which the child-ghost of Catherine Linton beats at the window crying, 'Let me in!'

items.title: Mock #12 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the author with the text :
(a) Rita Kothari — (i) The Queen's Hinglish
(b) Probal Dasgupta — (ii) The Indianization of English
(c) Braj B. Kachru — (iii) Translating India
(d) Baljinder K. Mahal — (iv) The Otherness of English
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: Rita Kothari wrote Translating India (a-iii, 2003), Probal Dasgupta wrote The Otherness of English (b-iv, 1993), Braj B. Kachru wrote The Indianization of English (c-ii, 1983), and Baljinder K. Mahal wrote The Queen's Hinglish (d-i, 2006).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q32
items.stem: Which of the following works of Milton seeks to adapt the form of Greek tragedy?
items.explanation: Published in 1671 alongside Paradise Regained, John Milton's Samson Agonistes is a closet drama explicitly modeled on the form and structure of ancient Greek tragedy, featuring a Chorus, messenger speeches, and strict adherence to the classical unities.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q33
items.stem:
Which among the following are not the genuine sources of the sublime as cited by Longinus?
A. Creation of imaginative feelings
B. The command of "full-blooded" or robust ideas
C. The inspiration of "vehement emotion"
D. Nobility of spontaneity.
E. The general effect of dignity and elevation.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: In On the Sublime (Peri Hypsous), Longinus identifies five genuine sources of sublimity: grandeur of thought/robust ideas (B), vehement and inspired emotion (C), figures of thought and speech, noble diction, and dignified, elevated composition (E). 'Creation of imaginative feelings' (A) and 'Nobility of spontaneity' (D) are not among Longinus's five sources; thus A and D only.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q34
items.stem:
A remarkable novelist of the English Modernist phase who wrote a short book on what the
novel is (and why it matters) remarked, “Oh dear, yes - the novel tells a story”.  Identify the
novelist :
items.explanation: Modernist novelist E. M. Forster delivered the Clark Lectures at Cambridge in 1927, published as Aspects of the Novel, introducing classic critical distinctions between story and plot, and between flat and round characters.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following journals in the chronological order of publication.
 A. Longman's Magazine

 B. Cornhill Magazine
 C. Blackwood's Magazine
 D. Bentley's Miscellany
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: These nineteenth-century periodicals were founded in the chronological order: Blackwood's Edinburgh Magazine (1817, C), Bentley's Miscellany (1836, D), The Cornhill Magazine (1860, B), and Longman's Magazine (1882, A).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q36
items.stem: Which of the following works is not written by Chinua Achebe?
items.explanation: Weep Not, Child (1964) is the celebrated debut novel of Kenyan author Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o. The other three works—No Longer at Ease (1960), Arrow of God (1964), and the essay An Image of Africa (1977)—were all written by Nigerian author Chinua Achebe.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :— Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A) : Dialects are the broad range of social as well as regional varieties.
Reason (R) : A dialect describes variations not only at the phonological level, but also at the levels of lexis and syntax.
In the light of the above two statements choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Both statements are true in sociolinguistics: dialects encompass both regional and social varieties (sociolects), and unlike an accent (which is purely phonological), a dialect involves lexical, morphological, and syntactic variations. However, (R) defines the linguistic levels of a dialect rather than explaining why dialects span social and regional groups.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q38
items.stem:
Bertolt Brecht's Mother Courage and Her Children presents the war-torn Europe as its
protagonist as she follows troops with her canteenwagon.
What is the real name of Mother Courage ?
items.explanation: In Bertolt Brecht's epic anti-war play Mother Courage and Her Children (Mutter Courage und ihre Kinder, 1939), set during the Thirty Years' War, the canteen-woman known as 'Mother Courage' is named Anna Fierling.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q39
items.stem:
Which of the following are correct:
A. Roddy Doyle - The Barrytown Trilogy
B. Abraham Stoker - Confessions of an Irish Rebel
C. C. S. Lewis - The Chronicles of Narnia
D. Brendan Behan - Dracula
E. Eoin Colfer - Artemis Fowl

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Roddy Doyle wrote The Barrytown Trilogy (A), C. S. Lewis wrote The Chronicles of Narnia (C), and Eoin Colfer wrote the Artemis Fowl series (E), whereas Bram (Abraham) Stoker wrote Dracula and Brendan Behan wrote Confessions of an Irish Rebel.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q40
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem: The pre-eminent evaluative criterion of F.R. Leavis’s Great Tradition is
items.explanation: In The Great Tradition (1948), critic F.R. Leavis identifies a profound, mature "moral interest in life" as the central criterion that distinguishes the supreme English novelists—Jane Austen, George Eliot, Henry James, and Joseph Conrad.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q41
items.stem:
Match List – I with List – II according to the code given below :
List – I
i. Annie John
ii. Tom Jones
iii. The Sorrows of Young Werther
iv. Vathek

List – II
1. Picaresque
2. Bildungsroman
3. Gothic
4. Epistolary

Codes : i ii iii iv
items.explanation: Jamaica Kincaid's Annie John (1985) is a coming-of-age Bildungsroman (i-2); Henry Fielding's Tom Jones (1749) employs a picaresque road-novel structure (ii-1); Goethe's The Sorrows of Young Werther (1774) is an epistolary novel (iii-4); and William Beckford's Vathek (1786) is an Oriental Gothic novel (iv-3).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q42
items.stem: The phrase "structure of feeling" is attributed to
items.explanation: Welsh Marxist cultural theorist Raymond Williams coined the phrase 'structure of feeling' (in Preface to Film, 1954, The Long Revolution, 1961, and Marxism and Literature, 1977) to describe the shared, lived values and emerging sensibilities of a specific historical generation.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q43
items.stem:
Which of the following are poems by Nissim Ezekiel that make fun of Indians' use of English?
A. "Goodbye Party for Miss Pushpa T.S."
B. "Philosophy"
C. "Very Indian Poem in Indian English"
D. "Jewish Wedding in Bombay"
E. "Poet, Lover, Birdwatcher"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Nissim Ezekiel's 'Goodbye Party for Miss Pushpa T.S.' (from Hymns in Darkness, 1976, A) and 'Very Indian Poem in Indian English' (C) affectionately satirize Indian English ('Babu English') syntax, progressive-tense overuse, and idioms.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q44
items.stem: In Ulysses Leopold Bloom works for a Dublin
items.explanation: In James Joyce's Ulysses (1922), protagonist Leopold Bloom works as an advertising canvasser (solicitor of newspaper advertisements) for the Dublin newspaper The Freeman's Journal.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q45
items.stem:
Choose the correct chronological sequence in which the following texts were published:
A. Madness and Civilization
B. The Archaeology of Knowledge
C. The Language of the Self: The Function of Language in Psychoanalysis
D. The Birth of the Clinic
E. Culture and Anarchy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Following English publication dates, the chronological order is: Matthew Arnold's Culture and Anarchy (1869, E), Michel Foucault's Madness and Civilization (1961 French / 1965 English, A), Jacques Lacan's The Language of the Self (1968 English translation by Anthony Wilden, C), Foucault's The Archaeology of Knowledge (1969 French / 1972 English, B), and Foucault's The Birth of the Clinic (1973 English translation, D).

items.title: Mock #12 · Q46
items.stem:
The label 'Diasporic Writer' can be
applied to
I.
Meena Alexander
II.
Arundhati Roy
III.
Kiran Desai
IV.
Shashi Deshpande
The correct combination for the
statement, according to the code, is
options: I, II and IV are correct
items.explanation: Meena Alexander (I) and Kiran Desai (III) are prominent Indian-American diasporic writers who lived and worked abroad, whereas Arundhati Roy (II) and Shashi Deshpande (IV) are Indian English writers permanently based in India.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q47
items.stem: What does deductive method of reasoning refer to?
items.explanation: Deductive reasoning is a top-down logical approach that begins with general premises or overarching principles and deduces logically necessary conclusions about specific, particular cases. Inductive reasoning, by contrast, moves from specific empirical observations to general conclusions.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q48
items.stem: Who among the following linguists proposed the terms, 'competence' and 'performance'?
items.explanation: American linguist Noam Chomsky introduced the distinction between linguistic 'competence' and 'performance' in Aspects of the Theory of Syntax (1965). Competence denotes an ideal speaker-listener's innate, unconscious knowledge of grammatical rules, whereas performance refers to the actual production and comprehension of language in concrete situations.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q49
items.stem:
Which of these does Meenakshi Mukherjee propose as the possible target readership of early Indian English novel?
A. A pan-Indian readership
B. A localized Indian readership
C. A British readership
D. The colonial administrator in India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In her seminal critical studies of early Indian English fiction (including 'The Perishable Empire' and 'Realism and Reality'), Meenakshi Mukherjee argues that 19th-century Indian novelists writing in English primarily addressed an audience outside India—specifically a British readership and colonial administrators in India—which shaped their explanatory and ethnographic narrative strategies.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q50
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT written by Walter Scott ?
items.explanation: Ivanhoe (1819), The Lady of the Lake (1810), and The Heart of Midlothian (1818) are celebrated works by Sir Walter Scott, whereas 'The English Mail-Coach' (1849) is a famous visionary prose essay by Thomas De Quincey.

items.title: Mock #12 · Q51
items.stem:
Match the List-I with List-II

items.stem:
[Reading Comprehension: Prose Passage]
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:

"One key development in the evolving discussion surrounding popular culture which occurred during the early twentieth century was the association of popular culture with the United States of America. Through Hollywood and associated modes of popular entertainment, USA was beginning to exercise international cultural influence. The term 'Mass culture' is particularly relevant in this context as it refers to both the effects of American culture as well as to a specific theoretical debate that emerged in America during the post-war period. Dominic Strinati contends in his An Introduction to Theories of Popular Culture (1995) that 'mass culture refers to popular culture which is produced by the industrial techniques of mass production, and marketed for profit to a mass public of consumers.' Such a view of popular culture argues that the industrial revolution produces a series of atomised individuals who had not only lost touch with the communities of shared interest to which they once belonged but that they had also been subjected to the process of mechanisation and alienation. This rendered them ripe for systematic cultural manipulation through uniform, mass produced formulaic products designed to evoke frivolous, escapist and superficial pleasures."

Question:
Systematic culture manipulation takes place through:
items.explanation: According to Dominic Strinati's argument in the passage, industrial mass production creates "atomised individuals" who become vulnerable to "systematic cultural manipulation through uniform, mass produced formulaic products," which he defines as mass culture. Thus, systematic cultural manipulation occurs specifically through the mass production of culture.

That imaginative prose should be the special and opportune art of the modern world results from two important facts about the latter: first, the chaotic variety and complexity of its interests, making the intellectual issue, the really master currents of the present time incalculable - a condition of mind little susceptible of the restraint proper to verse form, so that the most characteristic verse of the nineteenth century has been lawless verse; and secondly, an all pervading naturalism, a curiosity about everything whatever as it really is, involving a certain humility of attitude, cognate to what must, after all, be the less ambitious form of literature. And prose thus asserting itself as the special and privileged artistic faculty of the present day, will be, however critics may try to narrow its scope, as varied in its excellence as humanity itself reflecting on the facts of its latest experience - an instrument of many stops, meditative, observant, descriptive, eloquent, analytic, plaintive, fervid.

Which of the following is closest to what the author means by "less ambitious form of literature"?
options: literature responsive to heightened state of human perception
items.explanation: By the 'less ambitious form of literature' (imaginative prose as opposed to verse), Pater means a flexible, naturalistic literary medium responsive to the heightened state of human perception and modern intellectual curiosity.
